summary: This informational document asks that RFC 2754 be moved to Historic status. That RFC asked IANA to create and digitally sign routing registry objects when assigning addresses, to distribute a public key. In practice this was never done on the public Internet.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 2754 asked IANA to create and sign routing-policy objects when it assigned addresses, but that work was never done on the public Internet. This memo obsoletes that request and tells IANA not to carry it out.

questions: why was rfc 2754 moved to historic
subtitle: IANA is directed not to carry out the actions requested in RFC 2754.

tldr.problem: RFC 2754 asked IANA to create and digitally sign routing-policy objects for address assignments, but these actions were never done on the public Internet.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6254 obsoletes RFC 2754, recommends Historic status for it, and directs IANA not to pursue those actions.
tldr.outcome: The memo says RPKI technologies now provide an architecture for secure routing and implementing the old actions would require significant complexity.

facts.label: IANA direction
facts.value: Do not pursue the RFC 2754 actions

today: RFC 6254 is Informational and obsoletes RFC 2754, recommending that it be moved to Historic. The unit metadata lists no later RFC that obsoletes or updates RFC 6254.

sections.title: The Earlier IANA Request
sections.content:
RFC 2754 requested that IANA create a repository of Routing Policy Specification Language (RPSL) objects and digitally sign them. It also asked IANA to create and sign inetnum and as-block objects as needed for each address assignment.

The purpose was to distribute an IANA-held public key in software implementations of the Distributed Routing Policy System. The RFC 6254 introduction reports that this was never done on the public Internet.
sections.plainLanguage: The old RFC asked IANA to create and sign routing records when it assigned addresses. The memo reports that this did not happen on the public Internet.

sections.title: Why the Request Was Retired
sections.content:
A review of IANA protocol-registration activities found that the requested actions had not been completed. The memo says an architecture and infrastructure for secure routing using Resource Public Key Infrastructure (RPKI) technologies now exist.

It also says implementing the RFC 2754 actions would require significant complexity in light of the alternative technology. RFC 6254 therefore recommends Historic status for RFC 2754 and directs IANA not to implement its requests.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo says secure-routing technology based on RPKI now exists. It concludes that carrying out the old request would add substantial complexity.

sections.title: Address Terms and IANA Direction
sections.content:
The memo defines an allocation as an address block managed by a registry for making assignments and allocations. An assignment is a block or single address registered to an end user for use on a network or networks.

IANA is instructed not to pursue or implement the actions requested in RFC 2754. Since the intended signatures never took place on the public Internet, moving RFC 2754 to Historic is said to have no known impact on Internet security.
sections.plainLanguage: An allocation is a block managed by a registry; an assignment is an address registered to an end user. IANA is told not to carry out the old signing request.

references.text: Alaettinoglu, C., Villamizar, C., and R. Govindan, "RPS IANA Issues", RFC 2754, January 2000.
